ReviewProbe1Test > sec_PROXY_004_transferEncodingOnHttp10ResponseIsInvalidResponse FAILED
    java.lang.AssertionError: status (body: hello) expected:<502> but was:<200>
1 test completed, 1 failed
evidence.intent_output: 502 with onError receiving exactly one ProxyException of kind INVALID_RESPONSE; the chunked body is never decoded or relayed

findings.title: HTTP/1.0 backend response with Transfer-Encoding: chunked is decoded as chunked instead of rejected as faulty framing
findings.description: RFC 9112 §6.1: 'A server or client that receives an HTTP/1.0 message containing a Transfer-Encoding header field MUST treat the message as if the framing is faulty, even if a Content-Length is present'; §6.3 then requires a proxy receiving a response with faulty framing to close the server connection, discard the response and send 502. SEC-PROXY-004 is explicitly 'stricter than the RFC' and lists smuggling as its threat, yet ResponseParser.status() throws away the HTTP minor version and framing() decodes 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK / Transfer-Encoding: chunked' as chunked and relays 200 'hello'. A backend (or anything between proxy and backend) that frames differently from the HTTP/1.0 semantics is accepted here, which is the exact desync class the requirement exists to close; this is the only place the parser is laxer than the RFC.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the minor version digit in ResponseParser.Head (e.g. boolean http10 from line.charAt(7)=='0'); in framing(), after the bodyless check, throw invalid("Transfer-Encoding on an HTTP/1.0 response") when head is HTTP/1.0 and transferEncodings is non-empty. HEAD/204/304 stay bodyless first (FR-PROXY-014 AC-6 unaffected). Reuse the probe above as the regression test in BackendResponseParserTest.
findings.req: SEC-PROXY-004 (requirement statement: RFC 9112 §6.3 framing, stricter than the RFC; RFC 9112 §6.1)

findings.drop_reason: Comment wording only: LineReader accepts a bare LF as line terminator everywhere (RFC 9112 §2.2 permits it, no AC requires CRLF) and the proxy re-frames the body for the client, so no desync; the Javadoc 'chunk data not followed by CRLF' slightly overstates the check.
findings.title: ChunkedBodyInputStream Javadoc says chunk data must be followed by CRLF but a bare LF is accepted
findings.description:
'5
hello
0

' decodes without failure because lines.read(0) treats a lone LF as the terminator.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'CRLF or LF' in the class comment, or reject bare LF if the team wants the stricter reading.

findings.drop_reason: Intended and documented (ResponseParser.MAX_HEAD_BYTES Javadoc): interim heads share the 64 KiB budget so a backend cannot stream 1xx heads forever; AC-2 does not say the budget is per head, and the old MAX_HEADER_LINES cap is subsumed by the byte bound.
findings.title: Interim 1xx heads count toward the same 64 KiB bound as the final head
findings.description: A 103 with a 40 KiB Link header followed by a 30 KiB final head is rejected although each head alone is within 64 KiB.

findings.drop_reason: Micro-optimisation: the single-byte read() bridges allocate a byte[1] per call, but DefaultResponse copies with bulk 8192-byte reads, and LineReader's per-byte reads go through a BufferedInputStream bounded at 64 KiB per head.
findings.title: Per-call byte[1] allocation in read() of RelayedBodyStream and ChunkedBodyInputStream
findings.description: read() allocates a new one-byte array per call.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: keep a reusable one-byte buffer field.

clean_code.description: The control-character test 'c < 0x20 && c != \'\t\' || c == 0x7F' is written out in ResponseParser.status (188) and ChunkedBodyInputStream.chunkSize (105-110) and duplicates HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue; both loops can be '!HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue(...)' on the substring.
The single-byte read() bridge is copied verbatim in ChunkedBodyInputStream (41-46) and RelayedBodyStream (59-64).

ResponseParser.LineReader exposes a mutable package-visible field 'consumed' that callers in two classes (ResponseParser.charge, ChunkedBodyInputStream.nextChunk 90) read after each call; LineReader and Malformed are shared line-level infrastructure nested inside the head parser, coupling ChunkedBodyInputStream to ResponseParser. A small package-private LineReader class with a consumed() accessor (or a read that charges a budget itself) would remove both.

Collecting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding field values by lower-cased name is written twice: the request side in Proxy (704-707) and the response side in ResponseParser.read (104-109). The parsing of the lists now goes through FramingLists as the wave-11 audit asked, but the collection step could also live there (e.g. FramingLists.collect(name, value, cl, te)).
